summary.title: Game Physics Series
summary.one_liner: An index of Allen Chou's tutorial posts on game physics simulation and physics engine architecture, covering rigid body dynamics, broadphase and narrowphase collision detection (GJK, EPA), and sequential impulse constraint solving.
keywords: how do game physics engines detect collisions
how to write a physics engine
takeaways: The series covers motion dynamics fundamentals and physics engine implementation details.
Broadphase topics include an overview and a dynamic AABB tree.
Collision detection covers the CSO and support function, GJK, and EPA for contact generation.
Collision resolution covers constraints, sequential impulse, contact constraints, stability (slops and warm starting), and constraint-based physics.
summary.summary: This page is a table-of-contents index for a multi-part tutorial series by Ming-Lun "Allen" Chou on game physics simulation and physics engine architecture. It links to posts organized into sections: Motion Dynamics fundamentals, Broadphase (overview and dynamic AABB tree), Collision Detection (CSO and support function, GJK, EPA), Collision Resolution (constraints and sequential impulse, contact constraints, stability, warm starting), and Misc. topics such as half-edge support functions for polyhedrons. The page itself contains only the list of links and a short description, so the detailed explanations live in the linked posts. The listing notes it is included in codecrafters-io/build-your-own-x under "Build your own Physics Engine".
